items.title: An impurity can be replaced by one with a locally finitely presented morphism and a closed point of the fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that any impurity of a module above a point can be replaced by an impurity whose morphism is locally of finite presentation and whose specialisation point is closed in the fibre over the given point (statement lines 4513-4520, tag 05FX). The proof does two concrete things: it uses the separation lemma to build a locally finitely presented replacement morphism together with a closed subscheme that keeps the closure of the impurity point away from the special fibre, and then, using that the fibre is a Jacobson scheme, it produces a closed point of the closure of the original point at which the fibre of the closure is still empty so that the specialisation may be shortened. The Jacobson closed point step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
